title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks (Revised)
abstract: We measure the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop on verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we produced a single shared LLM proposal per task and compared: (1) baseline — the shared proposal recorded as the LLM-only output, and (2) guarded — the identical proposal validated and, if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation, subjected to at most one automated repair iteration. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided executor reports p = 1.00 under its exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention. Execution accounting: model_calls_used = 501, observed repair-stage calls = 1. We confirm realized per-cluster sample sizes matched the preregistered allocation (VLAN-change: 167; ACL-change: 167; static-route-change: 166) and that no confirmatory exclusions occurred. The single discordant episode (baseline fail → guarded pass) is archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl and deterministically locatable by filtering for baseline pass==0 and guarded pass==1; archived validator_trace and repair trace show the verifier reported >0 preregistered high/medium-severity violations on the shared candidate and the automated repair call converted that task to verified pass. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; marginal verifier+single-repair improvement on the composite pass/fail metric is therefore small, though the verifier corrected a rare concrete failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to NetOps tasks (intent→configuration translation, change planning, and programmatic repair). Systems and surveys emphasize that operational safety depends heavily on surrounding engineering—deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback—so operator-facing deployments commonly place formal verifiers in the loop [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. A common operational pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): the LLM proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks machine-formalized properties, and automated or human repairs address flagged violations. Despite this conceptual consensus, controlled measurements that isolate the marginal verifier contribution while holding the model’s proposal fixed are scarce. Practitioners need conditional evidence: when an LLM already produces high-quality candidates on verifier-modeled properties, how much incremental safety does a verifier plus a modest automated repair budget provide? We answer this narrow, operational question with a preregistered paired experiment designed to isolate verifier+repair impact under deterministic semantics.
sections.related_work: Deterministic and formal verification methods for network configurations (header-space analysis, route-model verifiers, Batfish-style analyzers) provide machine-checkable safety properties such as reachability, isolation, and update atomicity and underpin verifier-in-the-loop designs [Beckett et al., 2017]. Concurrently, recent NetOps/AIOps systems integrate LLMs for intent parsing and configuration generation while advocating guardrails for operational reliability (e.g., INTA, Confucius, other agentic NetOps frameworks) [INTA, 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate–verify–repair patterns appear across structured generation domains as a practical mitigation for incorrect or unsafe outputs [PoeTone; INTA]. Separate literature catalogs LLM failure modes (hallucination, overconfidence, tool-integration errors) and recommends verification or human oversight [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. Our contribution differs: a preregistered, artifact-backed paired ablation that holds the LLM’s shared proposal fixed and measures the marginal verifier+single-repair effect on a deterministic pass/fail metric.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered study cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026, freezing the research question, inclusion/exclusion rules, deterministic task seeds, estimands, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule prior to execution. Primary hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will reduce verifier-detected safety violations relative to the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired within-task). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations. The preregistration and artifacts are archived (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest).

Task corpus and stratification. A deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks was generated with deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 using preregistered seeds. Tasks were stratified per preregistration into: VLAN-change = 167, ACL-change = 167, static-route-change = 166. Deterministic replacement rules handled duplicates or excluded items; the run produced no confirmatory exclusions (analysis/exclusions = []). Deterministic_reconciliation.json documents task_count = 500 and that all consistency checks passed.

Generation semantics and experimental control. To isolate verifier+repair conditional on identical proposals we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false). For each task the pipeline produced a single shared LLM proposal; that identical proposal constituted both (a) the baseline LLM-only output, and (b) the guarded input validated by the deterministic verifier. The guarded arm invoked an automated single-repair call only if the verifier reported a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on the shared candidate. This intentionally excludes verifier-guided regeneration and measures the effect of verification plus at most one repair applied to the same initial proposal.

Models, adapter, and verifier. Requested LLM = gpt-5-mini called through the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (provider recorded as openai_responses); execution/model_configuration.json records parameters (max_output_tokens = 2000, single-attempt generation). The deterministic verifier used is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator-spec and violation-code→severity mapping archived). The guarded arm allowed up to one automated repair iteration per preregistration.

Statistical analysis and exact-test implementation. The preregistered confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes. The archived analysis executor implements this test by forming n = n10 + n01 (discordant pairs) and applying an exact binomial B(n, 0.5) test on n10 under the executor’s discordant-ordering convention; two-sided p is computed as p_two-sided = 2 × min{P(X ≤ n10), P(X ≥ n10)}, truncated at 1.0. We also computed paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (B = 10,000, seed = 1729) resampling whole task pairs with replacement. Missingness and retry policy: up to two automated retries for transient provider errors; execution stopped after processing the preregistered confirmatory pairs or when the adapter model-call budget was reached. All provider-call traces, prompts, seeds, and logs are archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The run completed with complete_pair_count = 500 and model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation = 500; repair-stage calls observed = 1). Aggregated per-condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.000). Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Exact-test and uncertainty. Using the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention described above yields two-sided p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts (n = 1, n10 = 1). Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The low baseline-failure prevalence (1/500) produced a ceiling effect that reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements relative to the preregistered power assumptions.

Discordant episode provenance (archival facts). The run issued exactly one repair-stage provider call and produced exactly one discordant pair (n10 = 1). The discordant episode is archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl and is deterministically locatable: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for entries where baseline scoring indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while guarded scoring indicates pass == 1; because only one such entry exists this returns the single discordant episode and its full archived traces. The archived validator_trace and the associated repair-provider trace show that the shared candidate initially triggered >0 preregistered high/medium-severity violations and that the automated repair call converted the task to verified pass (guarded pass == 1). For deterministic auditability the evidence bundle contains the per-task validator diagnostics, normalized configurations, repair prompts/responses, and provider-call traces; the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json confirm model_calls_used = 501 and repair-stage calls = 1.

Per-cluster realization. The realized per-cluster sample sizes matched the preregistered allocation (VLAN-change: 167; ACL-change: 167; static-route-change: 166). Deterministic task generation and the absence of confirmatory exclusions (analysis/exclusions = []) together yield a realized confirmatory set that follows the preregistered stratification; see execution/task_manifest.jsonl and deterministic_reconciliation.json in the archive for per-task assignments and seeds.

Representative examples. Representative per-task artifacts are archived for deterministic inspection (execution/responses and execution/scoring JSON artifacts). Example entries in the archive (representative_tasks) show medium- and hard-difficulty workflows where both baseline and guarded produced identical valid configurations; the single corrected episode’s full validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are available in execution/raw_results.jsonl and associated provider-call traces in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion:
Conditional operational interpretation. Under the constrained experiment—single requested LLM (gpt-5-mini), shared_initial_candidate semantics, deterministic verifier modeling a limited feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and at most one automated repair—the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals and the marginal measured verifier+repair benefit on the composite verifier pass-rate metric was small (0.002). This result is conditional on (a) verifier scope (properties the verifier models and marks high/medium severity), (b) shared-initial semantics (no verifier-guided regeneration), and (c) the synthetic, deterministic task distribution. The verifier still demonstrated corrective utility by converting a single concrete baseline failure into a pass; that episode and its repair trace are archived for deterministic inspection.

Design-choice implications. The shared-initial design isolates the verifier+repair effect conditional on identical proposals and aligns with deployment semantics that prefer repairing a human-reviewed proposal rather than regenerating alternatives. Alternative operational choices—verifier-guided regeneration, relaxed repair budgets, multiple repair iterations, or broader verifier scopes—may substantially change effect sizes and should be evaluated under their own preregistrations.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is strengthened by preregistration, deterministic seeds, automated replacement rules, and the absence of manual adjudication. Construct validity is limited by verifier coverage: success==no preregistered high/medium-severity violations is defined relative to the archived validator-spec; properties outside that modeled set (vendor-specific behaviors, dynamic protocol state) are not measured. External validity is constrained by a single model, synthetic tasks, and feature-limited verifier; no multi-vendor or production inference is claimed. Conclusion validity: preregistered power assumed baseline error ≈ 0.30; observed baseline error (0.002) created a ceiling effect and limited statistical sensitivity.

Operational recommendations. (1) Measure baseline proposal error prevalence on representative operational data before allocating repair budgets: when baseline verifier-scoped error is extremely low, marginal pass-rate gains per unit cost may be small. (2) Align verifier coverage with operator-critical properties and expand verifier modeling where needed; archived validator-spec maps violation codes to severities. (3) Select generation semantics consistent with deployment priorities: shared-initial reduces model calls and preserves the original candidate for human review, while regeneration-based guarded workflows may increase final-pass probability at the cost of additional calls.

Reproducibility and auditability. All artifacts required to reproduce the run are archived in the evidence bundle: preregistration (SHA-256 recorded in execution manifest), deterministic task generator and seeds, model_configuration.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl (per-task outcomes and the single discordant episode trace), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (per-task payloads and cluster assignments), provider-call traces, validator traces, analysis CSVs, bootstrap parameters, and deterministic_reconciliation.json. The run-level fields model_calls_used = 501 and observed repair-stage calls = 1 are recorded in the execution manifest. The initial master prompt used to start the autonomous run is archived (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).
sections.conclusion: We performed a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) designed to isolate the verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the executor’s convention). This conditional measurement documents a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is very high for properties modeled by the verifier and the verifier’s coverage is limited, a modest verifier+repair budget may yield negligible marginal pass-rate improvements on a composite pass/fail metric, while still being able to correct rare concrete failures. Practitioners should (a) measure baseline error prevalence on representative workloads, (b) align verifier coverage with operator-critical properties, and (c) select generation/repair semantics that match deployment priorities. The full preregistration, code, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection of every reported claim.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
